# Outpost

> Terminal-first remote development. Local workflow. Remote runtime.

Outpost turns a remote Linux host into a shared development environment you control from your local terminal. Run Docker Compose stacks, Kubernetes (kind or k3d) clusters, and lightweight Linux machines on infrastructure you own — without installing Docker, kubectl, or a local VM stack on your laptop.

## Primary pages

- [Home](/): Product overview, install command, capabilities, and workflow
- [Documentation](/#docs): Markdown docs for commands, guides, and configuration
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/degoke/outpost): Source code, issues, and releases
- [docs/ folder](https://github.com/degoke/outpost/tree/main/docs): Source markdown documentation

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/degoke/outpost/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

## Core commands

- `outpost host add` — register an existing Linux host over SSH
- `outpost host create` — provision a host on AWS
- `outpost init` — create project metadata (`--no-shell` for CI, `--no-compose` when Compose is unused)
- `outpost shell` — sync, start managed container, open interactive shell
- `outpost run -- COMMAND` — run a command in the project environment
- `outpost compose up`, `down`, `logs`, `exec` — manage Compose on the remote host
- `outpost app build`, `run`, `status`, `logs`, `stop` — Dockerfile application lifecycle
- `outpost open` / `outpost close` — forward project ports to localhost (`--port`, `--local-port`, `--service`)
- `outpost migrate --from HOST --to HOST` — migrate full project environment between hosts
- `outpost cleanup` — remove stale Outpost-owned project artifacts
- `outpost cluster up` / `down` / `status` / `env` — project Kubernetes (kind or k3d)
- `outpost machine` — project-scoped Incus container or VM
- `outpost invite create` / `join` — share host access with teammates

## Configuration

Outpost uses two `.outpost` locations:

- `~/.outpost/` — global CLI config on your machine (hosts, SSH keys, sessions). Not in your git repo.
- `.outpost/` — per-repository project folder created by `outpost init` (`project.yaml`, `.outpostignore`). Never synced to the remote host. Usually committed so teammates share the same project name and environment settings.

## Product facts

- Connects over SSH; no permanent Outpost agent on the server
- Creates one managed remote development container per project
- `init` is metadata-first; sync and container start on `shell`, `run`, or `compose up`
- Reads `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` for image, workspace, ports, environment, mounts, and build settings
- Cleans managed artifacts and retained logs according to project cleanup settings
- Supports existing hosts or AWS-provisioned EC2 instances
- macOS and Linux CLI
- Open source: https://github.com/degoke/outpost
